**Lisdexamfetamin (N06BA12)** is a medication used in the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Pharmacologically, it is defined by the ATC code N06BA12 and acts as a prodrug of dexamfetamine designed to provide an extended duration of action [^src3]. In the context of the Danish national healthcare system, it plays a significant role in the systematic quality measurement and monitoring of ADHD treatments.

Within the Danish ADHD Database (ADHD-databasen), Lisdexamfetamin is formally tracked as one of six core ADHD medications used to calculate [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] [^src1] [^src2]. This indicator measures the coverage of pharmacological treatment among children and young people with ADHD who are in treatment pathways [^src1] [^src2]. The tracking of this medication helps health authorities assess regional variations and systemic challenges in medical treatment practices across different departments and regions in Denmark [^src1] [^src2].

As the national database expanded its scope to include adult patients, Lisdexamfetamin was also incorporated into the newly introduced [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] [^src3]. This indicator focuses specifically on pharmacological treatment among adults with ADHD, utilizing data from the National Patient Register (LPR) and medicine statistics to evaluate clinical quality and evidence-based practice for the adult population [^src3]. By being a standard component of both Indikator 6 and Indikator 11, Lisdexamfetamin serves as a key metric in the political steering and clinical quality development of ADHD care in Denmark [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].
